prerequisites: the Kernel of a linear map
the Newton’s second law of motion

learning_outcomes.text: Introduction to the basic problems of dynamical systems theory as well as the discussion of some related formal models.
To understand the concepts of equilibrium point, orbit, periodic orbit, stability, chaos and to operate with them at least in some simple situations.
The incorporation of formal models in specific applications from different domains.

The application of the rules of organized and efficient work, of responsible attitudes toward the didactic-scientific domain, for the creative valorization of their own potential, respecting the principles and the norms of the professional ethic.

The use of some efficient methods and techniques to learn, to inform themselves, to do research and to develop the abilities for the valorization of their knowledges, to adapt to a dynamical society, and to communicate.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to dynamical systems (examples, notions, initial conditions, boundary conditions, examples, fundamental problems, physical models)
Linear differential equations (existence and uniqueness theorem, fundamental theorems)
Linear differential equations with constant coefficients.
Linear differential equations. Applications (Newton’s law of cooling, Pendulum equation, Harmonic oscillations)
Scalar first order linear differential equations
Linear differential systems
The dynamical system generated by a differential equation (main notions and first examples). Phase portraits of scalar equations.
Stability of equilibria (definition, examples, stability of linear systems, the linearization method). The nonlinear pendulum equation.
Phase portraits of planar systems.
Numerical methods for ordinary differential equations (Euler and Runge-Kutta numerical formulas)
Linear recurrences (difference equations) with constant coefficients (fundamental theorems, Fibonacci sequence)
Linear systems of difference equations (convergent matrix, complex notation)
Nonlinear scalar discrete dynamical systems (notions, examples, stability of a fixed point)
The logistic map. Euler numerical formula revisited.
Linear homogeneous differential equations with constant coefficients. General solutions and properties of solutions (periodicity, oscillations, boundedness…)
Introduction to Maple. Basic notions.
Linear differential equations (the method of undetermined coefficients, the Lagrange method).
The use of Maple to find the general solution of linear differential equations, to solve initial and boundary value problems and to study the properties of solutions
Linear differential equations.
The use of Maple to find the general solution to Euler equations and to linear systems. Power series method.
Phase portraits of scalar nonlinear dynamical systems and planar linear systems.
Orbits and direction fields of planar systems.
Stability of linear systems and of equilibria of nonlinear systems.
First integrals of planar systems around equilibria of center type.
Test. Introduction to linear recurrences.
Numerical methods. Nonlinear scalar maps.
Linear recurrences. Nonlinear scalar maps.
Test. Evaluation

assessment_methods.method: Interest and implication in each lab activity; one final test in the last lab

assessment_rules: Students must have presence at least at 6 labs and 5 seminars. To pass, students must obtain at least 7 points at the lab test and at least 15 points at the written exam. The minimum passing grade is 5.
